provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My body grows
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name body parts.
The pupils should be able to list body-building foods.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about our body parts.
Today we learn how our body grows.

Content:
Our body has bones, muscles and blood.
Bones make us stand tall.
Muscles help us move.
Blood carries food to all parts.
Milk, eggs and beans make us strong.
They help our bones and muscles grow.

Class activity:
Children will point to their bones and muscles.
They will name milk, eggs and beans.

Evaluation questions:
Name three body parts.
List body-building foods.
Why do we need food?

Summary:
Our body grows with good food and care.

topics.title: Dental care deep dive
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate brushing.
The pupils should be able to state when to visit dentist.

Introduction:
We use our teeth to eat every day.
We must care for them well.

Content:
Brush teeth twice daily.
Morning and night is best.
Spit out toothpaste.
Do not swallow it.
Visit dentist once a year.
Dentist checks teeth.

Class activity:
Children will practice brushing with toothbrush.
They will count to 20 while brushing.

Evaluation questions:
How many times do we brush daily?
What happens if we swallow toothpaste?
When should we visit the dentist?

Summary:
Good brushing keeps teeth clean and strong.

topics.title: Eye care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify good reading light.
The pupils should be able to explain eye rest.

Introduction:
Our eyes help us see the world.
We must protect them.

Content:
Read in good light.
Not too bright, not too dark.
Rest eyes between reading.
Look at green plants.
Close eyes for a minute.
Do not rub eyes with dirty hands.

Class activity:
Children will find good light in the classroom.
They will close eyes for 10 seconds.

Evaluation questions:
What kind of light is good for reading?
How do we rest our eyes?
Why should we not rub eyes?

Summary:
Eyes need light and rest to stay healthy.

topics.title: Ear care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ear care rules.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate cleaning.

Introduction:\Our ears help us hear sounds.
We must care for them.

Content:
Do not put sticks in ears.
Ears clean themselves.
Clean outside with a towel.
Do not shout near ears.
Ask for help when ears hurt.

Class activity:
Children will point to their ears.
They will wipe outside ears with clean towel.

Evaluation questions:
What should we not put in ears?
How do we clean ears?
When should we ask for help?

Summary:
Ears need gentle care to hear well.

topics.title: Germs and diseases
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how germs spread.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate hand washing.

Introduction:
Germs make us sick.
We can stop them.

Content:
Cough spreads germs.
Cover mouth with elbow.
Wash hands with soap.
After toilet and before eating.
Germs hide on dirty things.
Clean things keep germs away.

Class activity:
Children will cover mouth when coughing.
They will wash hands with soap and water.

Evaluation questions:
How do germs spread?
When should we wash hands?
What covers our mouth when coughing?

Summary:
Clean hands and covering cough stop germs.

topics.title: Malaria watch
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify malaria cause.
The pupils should be able to state prevention methods.

Introduction:
Malaria makes us feel weak.
Mosquitoes cause malaria.

Content:
Mosquitoes bite at dusk.
They hide in dark corners.
Sleep under treated nets.
Nets keep mosquitoes away.
Wear long sleeves at night.
Clear stagnant water around.

Class activity:
Children will pretend to sleep under nets.
They will flap hands like mosquitoes.

Evaluation questions:
What causes malaria?
When do mosquitoes bite?
How do we prevent malaria?

Summary:
Mosquito nets protect from malaria bites.

topics.title: Clean water and food
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify clean water.
The pupils should be able to explain food protection.

Introduction:
We need water and food to live.
They must be clean.

Content:
Drink clean water only.
Boil water if not sure.
Cover food from flies.
Flies carry germs.
Use clean plates and cups.
Wash fruits before eating.

Class activity:
Children will cover a bowl with a lid.
They will pretend to wash fruits.

Evaluation questions:
How do we know water is clean?
Why cover food from flies?
What should we do before eating fruits?

Summary:
Clean water and food keep us healthy.

topics.title: Traffic safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate road crossing.
The pupils should be able to identify safe walking rules.

Introduction:
Roads have cars and people.
We must be careful.

Content:
Look left, right and left again.
Check for danfo and cars.
Use zebra crossing to cross.
Walk on the footpath.
Hold adult hand when crossing.
Do not run on the road.

Class activity:
Children will practice crossing on a marked line.
They will look left and right before crossing.

Evaluation questions:
What do we look for before crossing?
Where should we cross the road?
What do we use to cross safely?

Summary:
Looking and using zebra crossing keeps us safe.

topics.title: My health card
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what a health card shows.
The pupils should be able to explain growth importance.

Introduction:
We have health cards at school.
They show our growth.

Content:
Health card has our name.
It shows height and weight.
Nurse measures us each term.
We can see if we grow well.
Good food helps us grow.
Exercise makes us strong.

Class activity:
Children will stand against a wall to measure height.
They will step on a scale to measure weight.

Evaluation questions:
What is in a health card?
Why do we measure height and weight?
What helps us grow well?

Summary:
Health cards show how we grow each term.

topics.title: Revision and health week
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall health habits.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate health practices.

Introduction:
This week we celebrate health.
We remember what we learned.

Content:
Nurse will talk about health.
She will show how to brush teeth.
Children will sing health songs.
Teachers will give certificates.
Certificates show good health habits.

Class activity:
Children will perform health songs.
They will show different health practices.

Evaluation questions:
What health habit do you like most?
Who helps us stay healthy?
What will you get for good health?

Summary:
Health week celebrates our good habits.
